recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is for FHIR core. If maxSize's datatype should be revisited, open a new Extension Pack change request rather than editing core or treating FHIR-33125 as an unresolved integer conversion.
issue_request: FHIR-33125 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core technical correction for Questionnaire/maxSize, asking to clarify whether maxSize uses bytes or MB and questioning whether a bytes-based value should be integer rather than decimal. The accepted resolution was to clarify bytes and correct the SDC example to use the decimal value 1024*1024 for 1 MB.
initial_application: Jira comments identify core application as Git Questionnaire-fixes ddcae05a32. Commit ddcae05a3224ff3ab56cefb5c8d224363f79a99b changed the maxSize short from 'Max size in MB' to 'Max size in bytes' and changed the definition to say 'maximum size in bytes', while leaving the value type as decimal. Jira comments also report separate SDC-side example fixes in commits dd06c20 and e629984.
additional_context: Commit dd468d4f1799dd79819315b211588ef1cf4586e0 later removed extension definitions from R5 core source. Current core source has only generic maxSize references in Questionnaire guidance and the element-extensions introduction, while /home/jmandel/work/fhir-extensions/input/definitions/multiple/StructureDefinition-maxSize.xml is the current maxSize definition source and says bytes in the description, short, and definition. The original Zulip thread and SDC Confluence minutes confirm the issue origin and Persuasive decision without adding a later datatype-change instruction.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit on the combined branch. No core source edit was made because the approved clarification is already reflected in the current source of truth outside core, and changing decimal to integer would exceed the FHIR-33125 resolution.

related_jiras.note: A separate Published Questionnaire extension context issue already represented on the combined branch; it is relevant only as broader evidence that Questionnaire-related extension definitions moved out of core and into the Extension Pack.
